Extremal Edges (EEs) are a special type of occlusion edge occurring when a 3D convex surface curves around to occlude a part of itself from the current viewing position (Ghose & Palmer, 2010; Huggins & Zucker, 2001a, 2001b; Palmer & Ghose, 2008).

Edge contours have been shown to be potent cues for relative depth and figure–ground segmentation where the region with the visible edge is perceived as closer (Palmer & Ghose, 2008), which would reinforce the existence of an occluder.
